# Mark P. M. Dean Website Design Analysis

## Hero Composition
The header features a centered profile photograph alongside the researcher's name and institutional affiliation at Brookhaven National Laboratory. This establishes immediate professional identity and institutional credibility.

## Navigation Structure
A horizontal top navigation bar provides access to key sections: About (homepage), People, Group Notes, Research, Openings, Publications, and Preprints. A search function (ctrl k) is also available, supporting discoverability across the site.

## Homepage Section Organization
The layout follows a logical progression: professional identity, research focus statement, then news updates. The research description emphasizes quantum materials and advanced X-ray techniques: "My research focuses on quantum materials, including high temperature superconductors, strongly spin-orbit coupled materials, complex oxide heterostructures, non-equilibrium states and topology in crystalline materials."

## Publication Presentation
Recent preprints and news items are listed chronologically with dates, titles, and links to full entries. Each news item highlights paper submissions and upcoming conference appearances with specific details about sessions and presentations.

## Typography & Color
The design employs minimalist styling typical of academic portfolios, likely using a clean sans-serif typeface with black text on white background for maximum readability.

## Density & Imagery
The layout maintains low information density with generous whitespace, a single centered profile image, and brief text blocks—characteristic of modern academic web design prioritizing clarity.

## Technical Framework
The site uses Jekyll with the "al-folio" theme, a popular template for researcher homepages offering built-in publication management and professional presentation features.

## Background
Zihao Sheng is a PhD student in transportation engineering at the University of Wisconsin-Madison who received a prestigious 2026-27 Grainger Wisconsin Distinguished Graduate Fellowship. He received his B.S. degree in Automation from Xi'an Jiaotong University in 2019 and his M.S. degree in Control Engineering from Shanghai Jiao Tong University in 2022.

## Research Focus
Sheng joined Civil and Environmental Engineering Assistant Professor Sikai Chen's lab in January 2023 and has focused on research that tackles some of the toughest challenges with autonomous driving. His research focuses on combining multimodal foundation models with reinforcement learning to enable autonomous vehicles to learn, reason and generalize from simulations into real-world scenarios.

## Research Pillars
Sheng's research is built on three pillars: leveraging vision-language models to enhance autonomous vehicles' ability to process and "understand" the world around them, embedding domain knowledge into the reinforcement learning process to make reinforcement learning-based driving policies safe and sample-efficient, and rigorously evaluating autonomous vehicle systems.

## Academic Output
Sheng has published 19 journal articles, nine of which he has written as the first author or co-first author, and his work has accrued more than 900 citations.

---
layout: page
title: Driving Simulation for Virtual Track Train
description: Conduct driving simulations of Virtual Track Train's hybrid control mode.
img: assets/img/drivingsimulator.jpg
importance: 1
category: Tongji University
related_publications: true
---

The virtual Track train (VTT) is a novel urban transportation solution that combines the advantages of trams and buses, operating on rubber wheels. Its core technology lies in a unique human/driverless hybrid driving mode. In the driverless mode, the train performs trajectory tracking by recognizing a virtual rail laid on the road surface, while in special conditions, manual control by a driver is required.

Due to its distinctive vehicle structure and control method, research on control algorithms and driving platforms for VTT is still relatively underdeveloped. Most related studies are focused on traditional automotive domains, which to some extent limit its promotion and application and pose potential safety risks.

This project aims to develop control methods for VTT based on an intelligent driving simulation platform, focusing on the following aspects:

1. Development of a comprehensive dynamic model for the VTT to support subsequent algorithm development and analysis.

2. Design of trajectory tracking control algorithms, encompassing guidance control and state observation.

These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:

# Hang Zhao's Academic Website: Design Analysis

## Hero Composition & Navigation
The page opens with a clean, minimal header featuring the name "Hang Zhao" and navigation links ([HOME], [PROJECTS], [ACTIVITIES]). A professional portrait photograph anchors the hero section, accompanied by institutional affiliation and Google Scholar link. The layout prioritizes simplicity over visual flourish.

## Homepage Section Order
1. Brief biographical introduction with research interests
2. Selected Projects (visual-heavy)
3. Teaching experience
4. Professional Activities
5. Talks and presentations
6. Current and past affiliations (logo gallery)

## Publication Presentation
Projects use a consistent template: thumbnail image/GIF, title, authors, venue/year, brief description in italics, and linked resources (Paper, Code, Project). This standardized format creates visual rhythm. GIFs and screenshots effectively convey technical concepts—for instance, parkour animations and autonomous driving system demos.

## Research Overview
The site emphasizes three core areas: "multi-modal learning, robotics, and autonomous driving." Publications span from foundational datasets (ADE20K) to cutting-edge foundation models (G0.5), demonstrating research evolution.

## Typography, Color & Density
Minimal color palette dominates—primarily black text on white background with blue hyperlinks. Typography relies on standard web fonts. Information density increases toward publication sections, using hierarchical heading sizes. The design favors readability over decorative elements.

## Imagery & Personal Touches
Beyond the portrait, projects showcase technical outputs: neural network visualizations, 3D reconstructions, and robot demonstrations. Logo affiliations gallery humanizes the CV, displaying institutional connections without excessive branding.

## Framework Hints
The page structure suggests static HTML generation or simple templating, with semantic markup supporting accessibility. No apparent JavaScript dependencies for core content delivery.

        {% include figure.liquid loading="eager" path="assets/img/5.jpg" title="example image" class="img-fluid rounded z-depth-1" %}
    </div>
</div>
<div class="caption">
    This image can also have a caption. It's like magic.
</div>

You can also put regular text between your rows of images, even citations {% cite einstein1950meaning %}.
Say you wanted to write a bit about your project before you posted the rest of the images.
You describe how you toiled, sweated, _bled_ for your project, and then... you reveal its glory in the next row of images.

<div class="row justify-content-sm-center">
    <div class="col-sm-8 mt-3 mt-md-0">
        {% include figure.liquid path="assets/img/6.jpg" title="example image" class="img-fluid rounded z-depth-1" %}
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-4 mt-3 mt-md-0">
        {% include figure.liquid path="assets/img/11.jpg" title="example image" class="img-fluid rounded z-depth-1" %}
    </div>
</div>
<div class="caption">
    You can also have artistically styled 2/3 + 1/3 images, like these.
</div>

The code is simple.
Just wrap your images with `<div class="col-sm">` and place them inside `<div class="row">` (read more about the <a href="https://getbootstrap.com/docs/4.4/layout/grid/">Bootstrap Grid</a> system).
To make images responsive, add `img-fluid` class to each; for rounded corners and shadows use `rounded` and `z-depth-1` classes.
Here's the code for the last row of images above:

{% raw %}

```html
<div class="row justify-content-sm-center">
  <div class="col-sm-8 mt-3 mt-md-0">
    {% include figure.liquid path="assets/img/6.jpg" title="example image" class="img-fluid rounded z-depth-1" %}
  </div>
  <div class="col-sm-4 mt-3 mt-md-0">
    {% include figure.liquid path="assets/img/11.jpg" title="example image" class="img-fluid rounded z-depth-1" %}
  </div>
</div>
```

34	  abstract={Ensuring safe decision-making in autonomous vehicles remains a fundamental challenge despite rapid advances in end-to-end learning approaches. Traditional reinforcement learning (RL) methods rely on manually engineered rewards or sparse collision signals, which fail to capture the rich contextual understanding required for safe driving and make unsafe exploration unavoidable in real-world settings. Recent vision-language models (VLMs) offer promising semantic understanding capabilities; however, their high inference latency and susceptibility to hallucination hinder direct application to real-time vehicle control. To address these limitations, this paper proposes DriveVLM-RL, a neuroscience-inspired framework that integrates VLMs into RL through a dual-pathway architecture for safe and deployable autonomous driving. The framework decomposes semantic reward learning into a Static Pathway for continuous spatial safety assessment using CLIP-based contrasting language goals, and a Dynamic Pathway for attention-gated multi-frame semantic risk reasoning using a lightweight detector and a large VLM. A hierarchical reward synthesis mechanism fuses semantic signals with vehicle states, while an asynchronous training pipeline decouples expensive VLM inference from environment interaction. All VLM components are used only during offline training and are removed at deployment, ensuring real-time feasibility. Experiments in the CARLA simulator show significant improvements in collision avoidance, task success, and generalization across diverse traffic scenarios, including strong robustness under settings without explicit collision penalties. These results demonstrate that DriveVLM-RL provides a practical paradigm for integrating foundation models into autonomous driving without compromising real-time feasibility.},

This paper introduces Sky-Drive, a novel distributed multi-agent simulation platform that addresses these limitations through four key innovations: (a) a distributed architecture for synchronized simulation across multiple terminals; (b) a multi-modal human-in-the-loop framework integrating diverse sensors to collect rich behavioral data; (c) a human-AI collaboration mechanism supporting continuous and adaptive knowledge exchange; and (d) a digital twin (DT) framework for constructing high-fidelity virtual replicas of real-world transportation environments. Sky-Drive supports diverse applications such as autonomous vehicle (AV)-vulnerable road user (VRU) interaction modeling, human-in-the-loop training, socially-aware reinforcement learning, personalized driving policy, and customized scenario generation. 67	  abstract={The Virtual Track Train (VTT) represents a novel urban transportation solution that combines elements of both road and rail vehicles. Currently, VTT has gained significant adoption in several cities in China including Yibin, Zhuzhou, Harbin, and Yancheng. Despite its growing usage, the unique structure and complex tire-ground interaction of VTT pose significant challenges in terms of tire wear, which has become a pressing issue. This study develops and validates a multi-body dynamics model of VTT along with a finite element model of its tire. The tire-ground contact behavior and boundary conditions are studied from various perspectives to calculate tire wear. The simulation results demonstrate that the internal pressure of the tires, the load of VTT, the pavement conditions, the inclination angle, and slippage of tires all have critical effects on VTT’s tire wear. These findings suggest that the operating conditions of VTT must be carefully managed to reduce tire wear and ensure safe operation. Furthermore, the research results of tire wear mechanism of VTT offers valuable insights for the optimization and maintenance of VTT.},

# Part 1 — Site-by-site analysis

## Group A: widely admired ML/AI/robotics pages

### 1. https://jonbarron.info — hand-written HTML/Jekyll (footer invites source reuse)
- **Hero:** small circular headshot, left; "Jon Barron" as H1; one line — principal research scientist at Google DeepMind + research areas; plain **text links** (Email, CV, Bio, Scholar, Twitter, Github), no buttons.
- **Nav:** none. Single long scroll with section headings: Research, Micropapers, Recorded Talks, Academic Service, Teaching.
- **Pubs:** full chronological list, **before/after thumbnail pairs (~160px)**, embedded video placeholders, **bold self-name**, venue + italic oral/award callouts, 1–2 sentence plain-language summary per paper, links to project page / arXiv / code / supplement.
- **Research overview figure:** no dedicated block — the thumbnails *are* the argument.
- **Type/color:** black on white, blue links, sans, minimal. **Density: high** — deliberately.
- **Personal:** minimal; dry wit ("Do not scrape").
- **Why it works:** every paper is instantly legible as a picture + one sentence, so a stranger understands the research portfolio in 30 seconds of scrolling. **Weakness:** no nav and no whitespace — punishing on mobile and hard to jump to a section.

### 2. https://lilianweng.github.io — Hugo + PaperMod
- Header is a **blog banner**, not an academic hero: "Lil'Log" + one line ("Hi, this is Lilian. I'm documenting my learning notes…"). Nav: Posts, Archive, Search, Tags, FAQ (5) + social icons (Twitter, Scholar, RSS, GitHub, Instagram).
- Reverse-chron post list: title, excerpt, date, **reading time**, author. Heavy whitespace between posts, neutral palette, no imagery.
- **Why it works:** ruthless single-purpose design — it is a writing site and never pretends to be a CV. **Weakness:** essentially no personal/academic identity layer; a reader can't tell affiliation or publications.

### 3. https://ysymyth.github.io (Shunyu Yao) — lightweight static
- **Hero:** circular photo left-of-center; "Shunyu Yao" + 姚顺雨 beneath; **tagline is four words: "I study agents."**; affiliation (researcher at OpenAI) in the About paragraph; icon links (email, blog, Scholar, GitHub, Twitter).
- Nav: anchors only (About, Selected work). Order: hero → bio → selected work → online talks → **recent readings**.
- **Pubs:** *selected only*, **no thumbnails, no badges**; bold title, authors with `*`, venue+year, inline text links.
- Monochrome + blue links, sans, generous whitespace, single column.
- **Why it works:** the four-word tagline plus a curated "selected work" list does more positioning than most people's three paragraphs. **Weakness:** zero visuals means the work is unscannable for outsiders — it relies on the author's fame.

### 4. https://www.jasonwei.net (jasonwei20.github.io redirects here) — Squarespace
- **Hero:** headshot, "Jason Wei", tagline "I am an American AI researcher", affiliation Meta Superintelligence Labs + history; links Twitter, CV, Scholar, email.
- **Nav: 4 items** — Home | Papers | Blog | Thoughts. Mobile toggle.
- Homepage: hero → career narrative → **research highlights (chain-of-thought, instruction tuning, emergence)** → talk video → papers (date-descending, `[date] [title] [links]`) → talks & media.
- Sans, black on white, generous whitespace, one photo.
- **Why it works:** the "research highlights" paragraph names his three contributions in plain words — a reader leaves knowing what he's known for. **Weakness:** paper list is a bare text index; no thumbnails or venues.

### 5. https://timdettmers.com — WordPress + Genesis
- Hero: name + tagline **"Making deep learning accessible."** Nav: Blog, Publications, About Me + category filters (Deep Learning, Hardware, Neuroscience). Blog-first: reverse-chron posts with date, comments, tags, excerpt + "Read more"; sidebar of recent posts.
- Text-focused, minimal color, moderate density, no hero imagery.
- **Why it works:** the six-word tagline defines a niche and the category filters let readers self-route. **Weakness:** dated WordPress-blog chrome (sidebar, comment counts) reads less like a research page than a blog.

### 6. https://ai.stanford.edu/~cbfinn/ (Chelsea Finn) — plain HTML/Markdown
- Hero: left headshot, name, email, affiliations **as hyperlinks inside the opening sentence** ("Assistant Professor … at Stanford and co-founder of Pi").
- No nav bar; document flow: intro → credentials → **prospective-students note** → link row (CV, bio, dissertation, Scholar, Twitter, lab) → news → talks → team → teaching.
- Research statement is a **single italicized sentence**. News is delegated to Twitter/lab site.
- **Why it works:** the early "prospective students" block and link row answer the two questions 90% of visitors arrive with. **Weakness:** no publication list at all on the page and almost no visual hierarchy.

### 7. https://rush-nlp.com (Sasha Rush) — lightweight static
- Hero: GitHub avatar + H1 name + **comma-separated tags** ("ML Researcher, Cursor, NYC") + contact. **Nav: 5** — Main, Group, Projects, Publications, raw-papers icon.
- Projects shown as **visual cards**: thumbnail + title + authors + venue/year, newest first. Black on white, sans at varying weights, generous whitespace.
- Self-deprecating asides ("somewhat regretfully, a twitter").
- **Why it works:** "ML Researcher, Cursor, NYC" is a three-token identity; thumbnail cards make the work skimmable. **Weakness:** inconsistent depth between Projects and Publications; the split is unexplained.

### 8. https://www.cs.princeton.edu/~danqic/ (Danqi Chen) — hand-crafted HTML
- Centered, text-first: name + **"How to pronounce?"** link + Chinese name as image → social icons → title/affiliations → contact → headshot mid-page → long bio.
- **Nav: 5** — Papers, Lab, Teaching & Service, Awards, Etc.
- Moderate-to-high density, formal academic typography, almost no imagery.
- **Why it works:** affiliations get top billing and the pronunciation link is a genuinely thoughtful accessibility touch. **Weakness:** photo placed *after* the bio breaks the hero; visually the most dated page in group A.

### 9. https://colinraffel.com — minimal static
- Hero: **grayscale headshot** + affiliations (Toronto, Vector, Hugging Face). Order: identity → roles → **lab mission → team roster** → publications → media → CV → blog.
- **Publications are not listed** — a link to arXiv instead.
- Information-sparse, very generous whitespace, one image.
- **Why it works:** puts the lab and team above self-promotion, which is exactly right for a PI recruiting students. **Weakness:** delegating publications to arXiv removes all curation — no visitor learns what matters.

## Group B: transportation / AV / ITS pages

### 10. https://www.huang-zilin.com/ — **al-folio** (the user's reference)
- **Hero:** left-aligned medium profile photo; "Zilin Huang" + Chinese name; Research Associate + department + university + office + email; **11 icon links** (Scholar, LinkedIn, GitHub, X, ORCID, WeChat, ResearchGate, Semantic Scholar, HuggingFace, DBLP, CV).
- **Nav: 10** — About, Research, Publications, Projects, Teaching, Talks, Services, Awards, News, Personal.
- **Order:** hero → social links → **research statement with a full-width "human–robot–society ecosystem" vision figure and three numbered research questions** → news (3–4, *with thumbnails*) → selected publications (9) → visitor counter.
- **Pubs:** teaser thumbnails, **bold self-name**, year + venue badge (TR-C, ICCV Workshop, JICV), 🔥 on recent work, PDF/code links, Chinese-language summaries, "+" co-author notation.
- Sans throughout; accents limited to red/burgundy Sky-Lab logo and gray institutional logos; generous whitespace; **news GIFs** (traffic animation).
- Personal: "Hi, thanks for stopping by! 👋", founding-member notes, **explicit "on the 2026–2027 academic job market"**, heavy emoji (📢 🎉 👏 🔥), WeChat.
- **Why it works:** the research-vision figure near the top converts an abstract bio into a single memorable diagram, and every publication carries a teaser image + venue badge. **Weakness:** 10 nav items and 9 "selected" publications dilute the word "selected"; emoji density is high.

### 11. https://ys-qu.github.io/ (Yansong Qu, Purdue) — **al-folio**
- Hero: **handwritten signature image** as a signature graphic, then "Ph.D. Student" + Purdue, contact/office, photo placed lower; 7 icon links + **WeChat QR modal**.
- **Nav: 8** — About, Presentations, Projects, Publications, News, Awards, Teaching, Services + CV.
- Order: intro + advisor → research focus → **internship call-to-action** → news → selected publications.
- **Pubs: animated GIF thumbnails**, bold self-name, venue emphasized, PDF + project page + BibTeX, preprint vs peer-reviewed separated.
- Research overview is prose only — **no figure**. Minimal color; imagery is research GIFs and **simulator screenshots**.
- **Why it works:** GIF thumbnails are the single highest-signal element for AV work — motion communicates a driving policy instantly. **Weakness:** the signature graphic and buried photo weaken the hero; 8 nav items for a PhD student.

### 12. https://zihaosheng.github.io/ (Zihao Sheng, same lab, UW–Madison) — Jekyll academic template
- **Hero:** centered circular photo; "Zihao Sheng"; "PhD Candidate at UW-Madison"; **tagline as pipe-separated keywords: "Autonomous Driving | Foundation Models | RL"**; 9 social links.
- **Nav: 3** — Homepage, About Me, Publications.
- Order: hero → About Me → News → **Selected Publications + "view all" link** → Honors & Awards → Education → Services.
- **Pubs:** left-side **animated GIF or static thumbnail**, bold self-name, **venue badges (ECCV, CHAIN, TRC, CVPRW, JICV)**, webpage/PDF/code links with **GitHub star counts**.
- Inline logo badges for UW–Madison, NVIDIA, Bosch. Emoji section markers (👨‍🎓 🔥 📝 🎖 📖 💡). Moderate density.
- **Why it works:** 3-item nav + "selected + view all" is the cleanest information architecture in group B; the keyword tagline positions him in six words. **Weakness:** no research-overview figure, so the three research pillars stay as text.

### 13. https://carlinds.github.io/ (Carl Lindström, Zenseact/Chalmers) — **al-folio**
- Hero: circular photo + name, minimal. **Nav: 3** — about, publications, repositories.
- Order: bio ("industrial PhD student at Zenseact and Chalmers… 3D perception, neural rendering") → news timeline → selected publications (11).
- **Pubs: animated GIFs + static thumbnails**, bold self-name, **venue badges (CVPR, ICCV, SIGGRAPH)**, arXiv + code + project site + BibTeX, newest first.
- Restrained color, light/dark compatible, balanced density.
- **Why it works:** a 3-item nav and a GIF-rich publication list — nothing else — and it reads as more senior than most 8-item pages. **Weakness:** no research-overview section at all; the reader must infer the thesis from 11 papers.

### 14. https://he-h.github.io/ (Haoyu He, CEE PhD candidate) — al-folio-like
- Hero: portrait + name + "Ph.D. candidate in Civil and Environmental Engineering" + institution; 6 profile links below the image.
- **Nav: 8** — Homepage, About, News, Publications, Educations, Awards, Invited Talks, Teaching.
- Order: bio → highlights → **publications grouped by year (2026→2022)** → education → awards → talks → teaching (résumé-like).
- **Pubs: no thumbnails**; bold venue, authors, `*` co-first, links (code | poster | news).
- Emoji section icons (🔥 📝 📖 🏅 💬 📚 📌); one photo; moderate density.
- **Why it works:** a crisp research identity sentence ("multimodal ML and large-scale spatiotemporal data modeling") anchors an otherwise CV-shaped page. **Weakness:** it *is* a CV in HTML — full year-grouped publication dump on the homepage, no curation, no imagery.

### 15. https://yongqidong.github.io/ (Yongqi Dong, RWTH Aachen / TU Delft) — Jekyll + **AcademicPages**
- Hero: portrait, name, affiliations as subtitle; 8 social links. **Nav: 6** — Homepage, Publications, Research, CV, Awards and Certificates, Teaching & Thesis Supervision.
- Order: hero → links → about + **recruitment statement** → chronological bio → news (dated, emoji, DOIs) → **Miscellany** → Archived Highlights.
- Publications live on a separate page; achievements appear embedded in news prose.
- Monochrome; moderate-to-high text density; one image.
- **Personal:** genuinely distinctive Miscellany — vegetarian/sustainable lifestyle, Tai Chi, meditation, reading, travel, plus three quotes.
- **Why it works:** the Miscellany section shows how to do "About me" with substance rather than a placeholder. **Weakness:** achievements buried in narrative; a visitor can't find the publications from the homepage.

### 16. https://wenzhuo-liu.github.io/index.html (Beijing Institute of Technology) — static Jekyll-ish
- Hero: photo + name in English and Chinese; nav is just Scholar + GitHub links.
- Order: About Me (advisors + focus) → News → Honor → **Review Services with journal impact factors** → Research Experience (internships) → Publications → Friendly Links.
- **Pubs:** thumbnails, bold self-name, title heading, italic venue+year, [Paper] [BibTeX] [Code], **ranking badges (JCR Q1, CCF A)**.
- Black on white, technical diagrams only, dense bulleted lists.
- **Why it works:** venue-ranking badges (CCF A / JCR Q1) are a field-appropriate credibility signal for the CN/ITS audience. **Weakness:** no real navigation; "Friendly Links" and IF numbers read as regional conventions that don't travel to US faculty readers.

### 17. https://nileshsuri.github.io/ (UMD, ECE/ISR — traffic optimization & AVs)
- Hero: nav bar → name + photo. **Nav: 4** — Home, Projects, Publications, Misc.
- Order: news feed (reverse-chron) → research interests → contact → bio → CV link.
- **Publications appear only as timestamped news announcements** — month/year + bold paper title + occasional link to a press story or award.
- **No demo videos, GIFs, or experiment visuals on the homepage.** Sans, generous whitespace, horizontal rules as separators.
- **Why it works:** the news-first layout signals momentum for an early-career student. **Weakness:** the single weakest publication presentation surveyed — a news feed is not a portfolio, and for an AV researcher the total absence of imagery is a missed opportunity.

### 18. https://hangzhaomit.github.io/ (Hang Zhao, Tsinghua — multimodal / robotics / AD) — static HTML
- Hero: name + `[HOME] [PROJECTS] [ACTIVITIES]` (3 nav) + portrait + affiliation + Scholar link.
- Order: bio (three areas: "multi-modal learning, robotics, and autonomous driving") → **Selected Projects** → teaching → activities → talks → **affiliation logo gallery**.
- **Projects use a strict repeating template:** thumbnail image or GIF → title → authors → venue/year → one italic sentence → [Paper] [Code] [Project]. GIFs show parkour and AV system demos.
- Black on white, blue links, standard fonts, density rises in the project section.
- **Why it works:** one rigid card template repeated dozens of times creates visual rhythm and makes a large body of work scannable. **Weakness:** "projects" and "publications" are conflated, and the page never states a thesis beyond three keywords.

## al-folio reference points
- Theme docs/showcase: https://github.com/alshedivat/al-folio and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alshedivat/al-folio/main/docs/SHOWCASE.md (150+ academic sites; BibTeX-driven publications with citation/altmetric badges, projects as a collection with galleries and video embeds, news collection, `ctrl+k` search, light/dark following system preference).
- Standout al-folio personal pages surveyed: https://maithraraghu.com/ (nav of 4 — about, blog, publications, CV; large name beside headshot; About → Research → Writing → News → publications last, reverse-chron with bold venue and rich link sets: arXiv/blog/code/slides/video; generous whitespace; a human detail about maths olympiads), https://markdean.info/ (centered photo + name + institution; nav of 6 + `ctrl k`; **one-sentence research-focus statement immediately under identity**, then news; very low density), plus https://carlinds.github.io/ and https://www.huang-zilin.com/ above.
- Note: https://platanios.org/ (listed in the showcase) has been taken over by an unrelated gambling site — do not use it as a reference.

# Part 2 — Synthesis

## 1. Recurring traits of the best pages

1. **One strong sentence (or fewer than eight words) directly under the name.** "I study agents" (ysymyth.github.io); "Making deep learning accessible." (timdettmers.com); "Autonomous Driving | Foundation Models | RL" (zihaosheng.github.io); "ML Researcher, Cursor, NYC" (rush-nlp.com); "I am an American AI researcher" (jasonwei.net). markdean.info puts a one-sentence research focus immediately below identity.
2. **Photo is small, ≤ ~30% of hero width, and is not the star.** jonbarron.info (small circular, left), ysymyth.github.io, carlinds.github.io, zihaosheng.github.io, colinraffel.com (grayscale, single image). Counter-cases that suffer: danqic (photo after the bio), ys-qu.github.io (photo pushed below a signature graphic).
3. **Short navigation — 3 to 5 items.** carlinds.github.io (3), zihaosheng.github.io (3), hangzhaomit.github.io (3), jasonwei.net (4), nileshsuri.github.io (4), maithraraghu.com (4), rush-nlp.com (5), danqic (5). The 8–10-item pages (huang-zilin 10, ys-qu 8, he-h 8) are measurably harder to scan.
4. **"Selected publications" genuinely capped and paired with a "view all" link.** zihaosheng.github.io does exactly this. Contrast: huang-zilin.com lists 9 "selected", carlinds.github.io 11, mczhi.github.io 12, he-h.github.io dumps every year — at which point "selected" stops meaning anything.
5. **Every publication entry carries a thumbnail, and in visual/robotics fields a GIF.** jonbarron.info (before/after pairs + video), rush-nlp.com, hangzhaomit.github.io, carlinds.github.io, ys-qu.github.io, zihaosheng.github.io, huang-zilin.com, wenzhuo-liu.github.io. Pages without thumbnails (ysymyth, he-h, nileshsuri, jasonwei.net, danqic) are noticeably harder for a non-specialist to skim.
6. **Bold self-name + a venue badge on every entry.** jonbarron.info, huang-zilin.com (TR-C, ICCV-W, JICV), carlinds.github.io (CVPR, ICCV, SIGGRAPH), zihaosheng.github.io (ECCV, TRC, CVPRW), wenzhuo-liu.github.io (plus JCR Q1 / CCF A), mczhi.github.io.
7. **A research-overview block with a hero figure, placed above news and publications.** The strongest single differentiator. huang-zilin.com has a full-width human–robot–society ecosystem figure plus three numbered research questions; mczhi.github.io has a three-direction research block (text only); jasonwei.net names its three contributions in prose. Most other pages skip it — and are weaker for it.
8. **News as terse dated lines, newest first, 3–5 on the homepage.** huang-zilin.com (3–4, some with thumbnails), carlinds.github.io, zihaosheng.github.io, markdean.info, he-h.github.io, yongqidong.github.io. Anti-case: nileshsuri.github.io, where the news feed *replaces* the publication list.
9. **One accent color at most, on a white background; color comes from content images, not chrome.** jonbarron.info (blue links only), ysymyth.github.io (monochrome + blue), hangzhaomit.github.io, danqic, wenzhuo-liu.github.io, colinraffel.com (grayscale photo). huang-zilin.com limits accent to the burgundy Sky-Lab logo.
10. **A rigid, repeated card template for every work item.** hangzhaomit.github.io (thumbnail → title → authors → venue/year → one italic sentence → Paper/Code/Project, repeated identically), jonbarron.info, rush-nlp.com, carlinds.github.io. The rhythm is what makes long lists readable.
11. **One plain-language sentence per paper explaining why it matters.** jonbarron.info and hangzhaomit.github.io both do this; it is rare and it is the biggest readability win available.
12. **Consistent institutional/affiliation logos, used sparingly.** hangzhaomit.github.io (logo gallery at the bottom), zihaosheng.github.io (inline UW–Madison / NVIDIA / Bosch badges), huang-zilin.com (UW–Madison, Purdue, CCAT, SHRC, TRAVELS), colinraffel.com (Toronto, Vector, HF as text).
13. **An explicit, early "what I'm looking for" line.** cbfinn (prospective-students note near the top), huang-zilin.com ("on the 2026–2027 academic job market"), ys-qu.github.io (internship CTA), yongqidong.github.io (recruitment statement), colinraffel.com (how to join the lab).
14. **Personal material has substance, not a placeholder.** yongqidong.github.io Miscellany (vegetarian/sustainable lifestyle, Tai Chi, meditation, three quotes), ysymyth.github.io "recent readings" (philosophy, physics, cognitive science), maithraraghu.com (maths olympiads), rush-nlp.com and colinraffel.com (self-deprecating asides). Note the pattern: these are *specific*, and none of them are emoji-driven.
15. **Emoji are near-absent from the top-tier pages.** None of jonbarron.info, ysymyth.github.io, rush-nlp.com, colinraffel.com, cbfinn, danqic, hangzhaomit.github.io, carlinds.github.io use emoji in the bio. Emoji clusters are concentrated in the CN/ITS student pages (huang-zilin.com, zihaosheng.github.io, he-h.github.io, yongqidong.github.io) — it is a subfield convention, not a mark of quality, and it reads as junior at density.

## 2. Anti-patterns on weaker pages

- **Publication list as a news feed.** nileshsuri.github.io announces papers as dated bulletins; there is no portfolio view.
- **Delegating publications entirely off-site.** colinraffel.com says "check arXiv" — zero curation, and the visitor learns nothing about what matters.
- **The HTML-CV.** he-h.github.io and yongqidong.github.io stack Education → Awards → Talks → Teaching → Service on the homepage; the page becomes a résumé transcription instead of an argument.
- **Nav inflation.** 8–10 items (huang-zilin.com, ys-qu.github.io, he-h.github.io) for a body of work that fits on two pages.
- **"Selected" that isn't selected.** 9–12 entries under a "selected" heading (huang-zilin.com, carlinds.github.io, mczhi.github.io).
- **Photo demoted below the fold or displaced by a decorative graphic.** danqic (headshot after the bio), ys-qu.github.io (handwritten signature occupies the hero slot).
- **Dated blog chrome** — sidebars, comment counts, pagination (timedettmers.com).
- **Regional-only credibility signals** — impact factors, CCF/JCR ranks, "Friendly Links", visitor counters (wenzhuo-liu.github.io, huang-zilin.com's visitor stat). These carry little weight with US faculty readers and cost hero real estate.
- **Zero imagery in a visual field.** nileshsuri.github.io works on AVs and traffic optimization and shows not one figure.
- **Conflating "projects" and "publications"** without explaining the distinction (rush-nlp.com, hangzhaomit.github.io).
- **Broken/abandoned reference links** — even the official al-folio showcase has rotted entries (platanios.org is now a gambling site), so the showcase should be treated as a starting point, not an endorsement.

## 3. Field-specific notes for transportation / AV / ITS pages

- **Animated GIF thumbnails are the field norm among the best pages and are near-mandatory.** carlinds.github.io, ys-qu.github.io, zihaosheng.github.io, hangzhaomit.github.io all lead publication entries with motion. Static diagrams (wenzhuo-liu.github.io, mczhi.github.io) are a clear step down: a driving policy, a merge maneuver, or a trajectory prediction is legible in two seconds of loop and illegible as prose.
- **Simulator screenshots are used as first-class evidence** (ys-qu.github.io explicitly; carlinds.github.io via neural-rendering/3DGS reconstructions). CARLA/SUMO/MetaDrive frames tell a reader what the experimental substrate is.
- **Maps and network/corridor visualizations are conspicuously rare** — none of the surveyed pages foreground them, even in the ITS group. This is an open differentiation opportunity for a transportation-engineering student whose work touches corridors or networks.
- **Venue badges do double duty in this field** because the venue set is split across two cultures: transportation journals (TR-C, TRB, JICV, T-ITS) and CV/ML conferences (CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS). huang-zilin.com, zihaosheng.github.io and carlinds.github.io all badge both, which is exactly how a cross-disciplinary reader is reassured.
- **GitHub star counts on code releases** appear on zihaosheng.github.io and mczhi.github.io and are a credible, field-appropriate impact signal for simulator/toolkit work — more persuasive than citation counts for a first-year.
- **A research-vision figure is the single largest visual differentiator in this group.** Only huang-zilin.com has one, and it is the main reason that page reads as more mature than its peers.
- **Emoji and WeChat/QR links are a strong convention in the CN-origin ITS cohort** (huang-zilin.com, ys-qu.github.io, zihaosheng.github.io, he-h.github.io, wenzhuo-liu.github.io) — worth keeping at low density for the audience it serves, but it should not dominate the bio.
- **Job-market / internship-seeking statements are standard and placed early** (huang-zilin.com, ys-qu.github.io, yongqidong.github.io).

## 4. Gap list — the user's current site (https://zhengyangwan.com/) vs. these traits

**Already satisfied:**
- **Short nav (4 items):** Home / Publications / Projects / About me — matches carlinds.github.io (3), zihaosheng.github.io (3), jasonwei.net (4), maithraraghu.com (4). Do not add items.
- **Genuinely selected publications (4)** — stricter than huang-zilin.com (9), carlinds.github.io (11), mczhi.github.io (12). This is a real advantage.
- **Publication thumbnails present** (landscape research previews), aligning with jonbarron.info, carlinds.github.io, rush-nlp.com.
- **News as 4 terse dated lines**, matching huang-zilin.com, carlinds.github.io, markdean.info.
- **Photo is right-floated and modest**, in line with the ≤30% convention (jonbarron.info, ysymyth.github.io).
- **White background, essentially no accent color** — matches the monochrome-plus-link-color norm across jonbarron.info, ysymyth.github.io, hangzhaomit.github.io, danqic.
- **Institutional logos inline** (UW–Madison, Sky-Lab, Tongji), as on zihaosheng.github.io and huang-zilin.com.
- **Multiple profile links present** (Email, CV, Scholar, ORCID, GitHub, LinkedIn, WeChat) — six-to-seven is the healthy range (jasonwei.net 4, jonbarron.info 6, zihaosheng.github.io 9); huang-zilin.com's 11 is excessive.
- **Education + Service sections exist** — appropriate for a first-year, though see below on their position.

**Not yet satisfied:**
- **No tagline.** The hero currently goes name → "Hello there!🤺" → bio. There is no equivalent of "I study agents" (ysymyth.github.io), "Autonomous Driving | Foundation Models | RL" (zihaosheng.github.io), or "Making deep learning accessible." (timdettmers.com). This is the largest single gap and the cheapest to close.
- **No research-overview block and no research hero figure.** This is the trait that most distinguishes the reference site (huang-zilin.com's full-width ecosystem diagram + three numbered research questions) from the user's page. The user has a Research block, but it lives on the *Publications* page rather than the homepage, and it has no figure.
- **No demo GIFs or simulator screenshots anywhere**, while every strong AV peer uses them (carlinds.github.io, ys-qu.github.io, zihaosheng.github.io, hangzhaomit.github.io). Static WebP previews are the current state.
- **No venue badges on publication entries.** Peers badge consistently (huang-zilin.com, carlinds.github.io, zihaosheng.github.io, mczhi.github.io). Venue text may be present but is not treated as a distinct visual token.
- **No one-sentence "why this paper matters" line per entry** — the trait that makes jonbarron.info and hangzhaomit.github.io outstanding, and which almost nobody in the ITS cohort does.
- **No "selected → view all" affordance** on the homepage publications block; zihaosheng.github.io is the model.
- **No explicit availability/intent statement** (internship-seeking, collaboration interests), which cbfinn, huang-zilin.com, ys-qu.github.io and yongqidong.github.io all place early.
- **Emoji density is high in the bio** ("Hello there!🤺", 🧐, 🏎️💨, 🥳) where the top-tier pages use none in the bio (jonbarron.info, ysymyth.github.io, rush-nlp.com, colinraffel.com, carlinds.github.io). Keeping them in *News* — as huang-zilin.com does — is the field-consistent compromise.
- **"About me" is a hobbies/travel placeholder**, whereas the pages that do this well make it specific and substantive: yongqidong.github.io's Miscellany, ysymyth.github.io's recent readings, maithraraghu.com's olympiad note. A placeholder page is worse than no page.
- **No per-paper resource link row beyond Abs/paper/BibTeX** — peers consistently offer project page / code / video / poster (carlinds.github.io, ys-qu.github.io, maithraraghu.com, zihaosheng.github.io).
- **Education and Service currently sit on the homepage below Selected Publications**, pushing the page toward the HTML-CV anti-pattern seen on he-h.github.io and yongqidong.github.io. The strongest peers (carlinds.github.io, markdean.info, maithraraghu.com) keep the homepage to identity → research → news → selected work and move résumé material elsewhere.
- **Projects page uses cards but is not visually tied to the publication template.** hangzhaomit.github.io's strength is one identical card template everywhere; the user currently has two different visual languages (cards on Projects, list-with-thumbnails on Publications).
- **No stated distinction between "Projects" and "Publications"** — the same ambiguity that weakens rush-nlp.com and hangzhaomit.github.io.

Sources: [huang-zilin.com](https://www.huang-zilin.com/), [jonbarron.info](https://jonbarron.info), [lilianweng.github.io](https://lilianweng.github.io), [ysymyth.github.io](https://ysymyth.github.io), [jasonwei.net](https://www.jasonwei.net/), [timdettmers.com](https://timdettmers.com), [ai.stanford.edu/~cbfinn](https://ai.stanford.edu/~cbfinn/), [rush-nlp.com](https://rush-nlp.com), [cs.princeton.edu/~danqic](https://www.cs.princeton.edu/~danqic/), [colinraffel.com](https://colinraffel.com), [sky-lab-uw.github.io/people](https://sky-lab-uw.github.io/people/), [ys-qu.github.io](https://ys-qu.github.io/), [zihaosheng.github.io](https://zihaosheng.github.io/), [carlinds.github.io](https://carlinds.github.io/), [he-h.github.io](https://he-h.github.io/), [yongqidong.github.io](https://yongqidong.github.io/), [wenzhuo-liu.github.io](https://wenzhuo-liu.github.io/index.html), [nileshsuri.github.io](https://nileshsuri.github.io/), [mczhi.github.io](https://mczhi.github.io/), [hangzhaomit.github.io](https://hangzhaomit.github.io/), [maithraraghu.com](https://maithraraghu.com/), [markdean.info](https://markdean.info/), [al-folio](https://github.com/alshedivat/al-folio), [al-folio SHOWCASE.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alshedivat/al-folio/main/docs/SHOWCASE.md), [zhengyangwan.com](https://zhengyangwan.com/)

# Part 1 — Site-by-site analysis

## Group A: widely admired ML/AI/robotics pages

### 1. https://jonbarron.info — hand-written HTML/Jekyll (footer invites source reuse)
- **Hero:** small circular headshot, left; "Jon Barron" as H1; one line — principal research scientist at Google DeepMind + research areas; plain **text links** (Email, CV, Bio, Scholar, Twitter, Github), no buttons.
- **Nav:** none. Single long scroll with section headings: Research, Micropapers, Recorded Talks, Academic Service, Teaching.
- **Pubs:** full chronological list, **before/after thumbnail pairs (~160px)**, embedded video placeholders, **bold self-name**, venue + italic oral/award callouts, 1–2 sentence plain-language summary per paper, links to project page / arXiv / code / supplement.
- **Research overview figure:** no dedicated block — the thumbnails *are* the argument.
- **Type/color:** black on white, blue links, sans, minimal. **Density: high** — deliberately.
- **Personal:** minimal; dry wit ("Do not scrape").
- **Why it works:** every paper is instantly legible as a picture + one sentence, so a stranger understands the research portfolio in 30 seconds of scrolling. **Weakness:** no nav and no whitespace — punishing on mobile and hard to jump to a section.

### 2. https://lilianweng.github.io — Hugo + PaperMod
- Header is a **blog banner**, not an academic hero: "Lil'Log" + one line ("Hi, this is Lilian. I'm documenting my learning notes…"). Nav: Posts, Archive, Search, Tags, FAQ (5) + social icons (Twitter, Scholar, RSS, GitHub, Instagram).
- Reverse-chron post list: title, excerpt, date, **reading time**, author. Heavy whitespace between posts, neutral palette, no imagery.
- **Why it works:** ruthless single-purpose design — it is a writing site and never pretends to be a CV. **Weakness:** essentially no personal/academic identity layer; a reader can't tell affiliation or publications.

### 3. https://ysymyth.github.io (Shunyu Yao) — lightweight static
- **Hero:** circular photo left-of-center; "Shunyu Yao" + 姚顺雨 beneath; **tagline is four words: "I study agents."**; affiliation (researcher at OpenAI) in the About paragraph; icon links (email, blog, Scholar, GitHub, Twitter).
- Nav: anchors only (About, Selected work). Order: hero → bio → selected work → online talks → **recent readings**.
- **Pubs:** *selected only*, **no thumbnails, no badges**; bold title, authors with `*`, venue+year, inline text links.
- Monochrome + blue links, sans, generous whitespace, single column.
- **Why it works:** the four-word tagline plus a curated "selected work" list does more positioning than most people's three paragraphs. **Weakness:** zero visuals means the work is unscannable for outsiders — it relies on the author's fame.

### 4. https://www.jasonwei.net (jasonwei20.github.io redirects here) — Squarespace
- **Hero:** headshot, "Jason Wei", tagline "I am an American AI researcher", affiliation Meta Superintelligence Labs + history; links Twitter, CV, Scholar, email.
- **Nav: 4 items** — Home | Papers | Blog | Thoughts. Mobile toggle.
- Homepage: hero → career narrative → **research highlights (chain-of-thought, instruction tuning, emergence)** → talk video → papers (date-descending, `[date] [title] [links]`) → talks &amp; media.
- Sans, black on white, generous whitespace, one photo.
- **Why it works:** the "research highlights" paragraph names his three contributions in plain words — a reader leaves knowing what he's known for. **Weakness:** paper list is a bare text index; no thumbnails or venues.

### 5. https://timdettmers.com — WordPress + Genesis
- Hero: name + tagline **"Making deep learning accessible."** Nav: Blog, Publications, About Me + category filters (Deep Learning, Hardware, Neuroscience). Blog-first: reverse-chron posts with date, comments, tags, excerpt + "Read more"; sidebar of recent posts.
- Text-focused, minimal color, moderate density, no hero imagery.
- **Why it works:** the six-word tagline defines a niche and the category filters let readers self-route. **Weakness:** dated WordPress-blog chrome (sidebar, comment counts) reads less like a research page than a blog.

### 6. https://ai.stanford.edu/~cbfinn/ (Chelsea Finn) — plain HTML/Markdown
- Hero: left headshot, name, email, affiliations **as hyperlinks inside the opening sentence** ("Assistant Professor … at Stanford and co-founder of Pi").
- No nav bar; document flow: intro → credentials → **prospective-students note** → link row (CV, bio, dissertation, Scholar, Twitter, lab) → news → talks → team → teaching.
- Research statement is a **single italicized sentence**. News is delegated to Twitter/lab site.
- **Why it works:** the early "prospective students" block and link row answer the two questions 90% of visitors arrive with. **Weakness:** no publication list at all on the page and almost no visual hierarchy.

### 7. https://rush-nlp.com (Sasha Rush) — lightweight static
- Hero: GitHub avatar + H1 name + **comma-separated tags** ("ML Researcher, Cursor, NYC") + contact. **Nav: 5** — Main, Group, Projects, Publications, raw-papers icon.
- Projects shown as **visual cards**: thumbnail + title + authors + venue/year, newest first. Black on white, sans at varying weights, generous whitespace.
- Self-deprecating asides ("somewhat regretfully, a twitter").
- **Why it works:** "ML Researcher, Cursor, NYC" is a three-token identity; thumbnail cards make the work skimmable. **Weakness:** inconsistent depth between Projects and Publications; the split is unexplained.

### 8. https://www.cs.princeton.edu/~danqic/ (Danqi Chen) — hand-crafted HTML
- Centered, text-first: name + **"How to pronounce?"** link + Chinese name as image → social icons → title/affiliations → contact → headshot mid-page → long bio.
- **Nav: 5** — Papers, Lab, Teaching &amp; Service, Awards, Etc.
- Moderate-to-high density, formal academic typography, almost no imagery.
- **Why it works:** affiliations get top billing and the pronunciation link is a genuinely thoughtful accessibility touch. **Weakness:** photo placed *after* the bio breaks the hero; visually the most dated page in group A.

### 9. https://colinraffel.com — minimal static
- Hero: **grayscale headshot** + affiliations (Toronto, Vector, Hugging Face). Order: identity → roles → **lab mission → team roster** → publications → media → CV → blog.
- **Publications are not listed** — a link to arXiv instead.
- Information-sparse, very generous whitespace, one image.
- **Why it works:** puts the lab and team above self-promotion, which is exactly right for a PI recruiting students. **Weakness:** delegating publications to arXiv removes all curation — no visitor learns what matters.

## Group B: transportation / AV / ITS pages

### 10. https://www.huang-zilin.com/ — **al-folio** (the user's reference)
- **Hero:** left-aligned medium profile photo; "Zilin Huang" + Chinese name; Research Associate + department + university + office + email; **11 icon links** (Scholar, LinkedIn, GitHub, X, ORCID, WeChat, ResearchGate, Semantic Scholar, HuggingFace, DBLP, CV).
- **Nav: 10** — About, Research, Publications, Projects, Teaching, Talks, Services, Awards, News, Personal.
- **Order:** hero → social links → **research statement with a full-width "human–robot–society ecosystem" vision figure and three numbered research questions** → news (3–4, *with thumbnails*) → selected publications (9) → visitor counter.
- **Pubs:** teaser thumbnails, **bold self-name**, year + venue badge (TR-C, ICCV Workshop, JICV), 🔥 on recent work, PDF/code links, Chinese-language summaries, "+" co-author notation.
- Sans throughout; accents limited to red/burgundy Sky-Lab logo and gray institutional logos; generous whitespace; **news GIFs** (traffic animation).
- Personal: "Hi, thanks for stopping by! 👋", founding-member notes, **explicit "on the 2026–2027 academic job market"**, heavy emoji (📢 🎉 👏 🔥), WeChat.
- **Why it works:** the research-vision figure near the top converts an abstract bio into a single memorable diagram, and every publication carries a teaser image + venue badge. **Weakness:** 10 nav items and 9 "selected" publications dilute the word "selected"; emoji density is high.

### 11. https://ys-qu.github.io/ (Yansong Qu, Purdue) — **al-folio**
- Hero: **handwritten signature image** as a signature graphic, then "Ph.D. Student" + Purdue, contact/office, photo placed lower; 7 icon links + **WeChat QR modal**.
- **Nav: 8** — About, Presentations, Projects, Publications, News, Awards, Teaching, Services + CV.
- Order: intro + advisor → research focus → **internship call-to-action** → news → selected publications.
- **Pubs: animated GIF thumbnails**, bold self-name, venue emphasized, PDF + project page + BibTeX, preprint vs peer-reviewed separated.
- Research overview is prose only — **no figure**. Minimal color; imagery is research GIFs and **simulator screenshots**.
- **Why it works:** GIF thumbnails are the single highest-signal element for AV work — motion communicates a driving policy instantly. **Weakness:** the signature graphic and buried photo weaken the hero; 8 nav items for a PhD student.

### 12. https://zihaosheng.github.io/ (Zihao Sheng, same lab, UW–Madison) — Jekyll academic template
- **Hero:** centered circular photo; "Zihao Sheng"; "PhD Candidate at UW-Madison"; **tagline as pipe-separated keywords: "Autonomous Driving | Foundation Models | RL"**; 9 social links.
- **Nav: 3** — Homepage, About Me, Publications.
- Order: hero → About Me → News → **Selected Publications + "view all" link** → Honors &amp; Awards → Education → Services.
- **Pubs:** left-side **animated GIF or static thumbnail**, bold self-name, **venue badges (ECCV, CHAIN, TRC, CVPRW, JICV)**, webpage/PDF/code links with **GitHub star counts**.
- Inline logo badges for UW–Madison, NVIDIA, Bosch. Emoji section markers (👨‍🎓 🔥 📝 🎖 📖 💡). Moderate density.
- **Why it works:** 3-item nav + "selected + view all" is the cleanest information architecture in group B; the keyword tagline positions him in six words. **Weakness:** no research-overview figure, so the three research pillars stay as text.

### 13. https://carlinds.github.io/ (Carl Lindström, Zenseact/Chalmers) — **al-folio**
- Hero: circular photo + name, minimal. **Nav: 3** — about, publications, repositories.
- Order: bio ("industrial PhD student at Zenseact and Chalmers… 3D perception, neural rendering") → news timeline → selected publications (11).
- **Pubs: animated GIFs + static thumbnails**, bold self-name, **venue badges (CVPR, ICCV, SIGGRAPH)**, arXiv + code + project site + BibTeX, newest first.
- Restrained color, light/dark compatible, balanced density.
- **Why it works:** a 3-item nav and a GIF-rich publication list — nothing else — and it reads as more senior than most 8-item pages. **Weakness:** no research-overview section at all; the reader must infer the thesis from 11 papers.

### 14. https://he-h.github.io/ (Haoyu He, CEE PhD candidate) — al-folio-like
- Hero: portrait + name + "Ph.D. candidate in Civil and Environmental Engineering" + institution; 6 profile links below the image.
- **Nav: 8** — Homepage, About, News, Publications, Educations, Awards, Invited Talks, Teaching.
- Order: bio → highlights → **publications grouped by year (2026→2022)** → education → awards → talks → teaching (résumé-like).
- **Pubs: no thumbnails**; bold venue, authors, `*` co-first, links (code | poster | news).
- Emoji section icons (🔥 📝 📖 🏅 💬 📚 📌); one photo; moderate density.
- **Why it works:** a crisp research identity sentence ("multimodal ML and large-scale spatiotemporal data modeling") anchors an otherwise CV-shaped page. **Weakness:** it *is* a CV in HTML — full year-grouped publication dump on the homepage, no curation, no imagery.

### 15. https://yongqidong.github.io/ (Yongqi Dong, RWTH Aachen / TU Delft) — Jekyll + **AcademicPages**
- Hero: portrait, name, affiliations as subtitle; 8 social links. **Nav: 6** — Homepage, Publications, Research, CV, Awards and Certificates, Teaching &amp; Thesis Supervision.
- Order: hero → links → about + **recruitment statement** → chronological bio → news (dated, emoji, DOIs) → **Miscellany** → Archived Highlights.
- Publications live on a separate page; achievements appear embedded in news prose.
- Monochrome; moderate-to-high text density; one image.
- **Personal:** genuinely distinctive Miscellany — vegetarian/sustainable lifestyle, Tai Chi, meditation, reading, travel, plus three quotes.
- **Why it works:** the Miscellany section shows how to do "About me" with substance rather than a placeholder. **Weakness:** achievements buried in narrative; a visitor can't find the publications from the homepage.

### 16. https://wenzhuo-liu.github.io/index.html (Beijing Institute of Technology) — static Jekyll-ish
- Hero: photo + name in English and Chinese; nav is just Scholar + GitHub links.
- Order: About Me (advisors + focus) → News → Honor → **Review Services with journal impact factors** → Research Experience (internships) → Publications → Friendly Links.
- **Pubs:** thumbnails, bold self-name, title heading, italic venue+year, [Paper] [BibTeX] [Code], **ranking badges (JCR Q1, CCF A)**.
- Black on white, technical diagrams only, dense bulleted lists.
- **Why it works:** venue-ranking badges (CCF A / JCR Q1) are a field-appropriate credibility signal for the CN/ITS audience. **Weakness:** no real navigation; "Friendly Links" and IF numbers read as regional conventions that don't travel to US faculty readers.

### 17. https://nileshsuri.github.io/ (UMD, ECE/ISR — traffic optimization &amp; AVs)
- Hero: nav bar → name + photo. **Nav: 4** — Home, Projects, Publications, Misc.
- Order: news feed (reverse-chron) → research interests → contact → bio → CV link.
- **Publications appear only as timestamped news announcements** — month/year + bold paper title + occasional link to a press story or award.
- **No demo videos, GIFs, or experiment visuals on the homepage.** Sans, generous whitespace, horizontal rules as separators.
- **Why it works:** the news-first layout signals momentum for an early-career student. **Weakness:** the single weakest publication presentation surveyed — a news feed is not a portfolio, and for an AV researcher the total absence of imagery is a missed opportunity.

### 18. https://hangzhaomit.github.io/ (Hang Zhao, Tsinghua — multimodal / robotics / AD) — static HTML
- Hero: name + `[HOME] [PROJECTS] [ACTIVITIES]` (3 nav) + portrait + affiliation + Scholar link.
- Order: bio (three areas: "multi-modal learning, robotics, and autonomous driving") → **Selected Projects** → teaching → activities → talks → **affiliation logo gallery**.
- **Projects use a strict repeating template:** thumbnail image or GIF → title → authors → venue/year → one italic sentence → [Paper] [Code] [Project]. GIFs show parkour and AV system demos.
- Black on white, blue links, standard fonts, density rises in the project section.
- **Why it works:** one rigid card template repeated dozens of times creates visual rhythm and makes a large body of work scannable. **Weakness:** "projects" and "publications" are conflated, and the page never states a thesis beyond three keywords.

## al-folio reference points
- Theme docs/showcase: https://github.com/alshedivat/al-folio and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alshedivat/al-folio/main/docs/SHOWCASE.md (150+ academic sites; BibTeX-driven publications with citation/altmetric badges, projects as a collection with galleries and video embeds, news collection, `ctrl+k` search, light/dark following system preference).
- Standout al-folio personal pages surveyed: https://maithraraghu.com/ (nav of 4 — about, blog, publications, CV; large name beside headshot; About → Research → Writing → News → publications last, reverse-chron with bold venue and rich link sets: arXiv/blog/code/slides/video; generous whitespace; a human detail about maths olympiads), https://markdean.info/ (centered photo + name + institution; nav of 6 + `ctrl k`; **one-sentence research-focus statement immediately under identity**, then news; very low density), plus https://carlinds.github.io/ and https://www.huang-zilin.com/ above.
- Note: https://platanios.org/ (listed in the showcase) has been taken over by an unrelated gambling site — do not use it as a reference.

# Part 2 — Synthesis

## 1. Recurring traits of the best pages

1. **One strong sentence (or fewer than eight words) directly under the name.** "I study agents" (ysymyth.github.io); "Making deep learning accessible." (timdettmers.com); "Autonomous Driving | Foundation Models | RL" (zihaosheng.github.io); "ML Researcher, Cursor, NYC" (rush-nlp.com); "I am an American AI researcher" (jasonwei.net). markdean.info puts a one-sentence research focus immediately below identity.
2. **Photo is small, ≤ ~30% of hero width, and is not the star.** jonbarron.info (small circular, left), ysymyth.github.io, carlinds.github.io, zihaosheng.github.io, colinraffel.com (grayscale, single image). Counter-cases that suffer: danqic (photo after the bio), ys-qu.github.io (photo pushed below a signature graphic).
3. **Short navigation — 3 to 5 items.** carlinds.github.io (3), zihaosheng.github.io (3), hangzhaomit.github.io (3), jasonwei.net (4), nileshsuri.github.io (4), maithraraghu.com (4), rush-nlp.com (5), danqic (5). The 8–10-item pages (huang-zilin 10, ys-qu 8, he-h 8) are measurably harder to scan.
4. **"Selected publications" genuinely capped and paired with a "view all" link.** zihaosheng.github.io does exactly this. Contrast: huang-zilin.com lists 9 "selected", carlinds.github.io 11, mczhi.github.io 12, he-h.github.io dumps every year — at which point "selected" stops meaning anything.
5. **Every publication entry carries a thumbnail, and in visual/robotics fields a GIF.** jonbarron.info (before/after pairs + video), rush-nlp.com, hangzhaomit.github.io, carlinds.github.io, ys-qu.github.io, zihaosheng.github.io, huang-zilin.com, wenzhuo-liu.github.io. Pages without thumbnails (ysymyth, he-h, nileshsuri, jasonwei.net, danqic) are noticeably harder for a non-specialist to skim.
6. **Bold self-name + a venue badge on every entry.** jonbarron.info, huang-zilin.com (TR-C, ICCV-W, JICV), carlinds.github.io (CVPR, ICCV, SIGGRAPH), zihaosheng.github.io (ECCV, TRC, CVPRW), wenzhuo-liu.github.io (plus JCR Q1 / CCF A), mczhi.github.io.
7. **A research-overview block with a hero figure, placed above news and publications.** The strongest single differentiator. huang-zilin.com has a full-width human–robot–society ecosystem figure plus three numbered research questions; mczhi.github.io has a three-direction research block (text only); jasonwei.net names its three contributions in prose. Most other pages skip it — and are weaker for it.
8. **News as terse dated lines, newest first, 3–5 on the homepage.** huang-zilin.com (3–4, some with thumbnails), carlinds.github.io, zihaosheng.github.io, markdean.info, he-h.github.io, yongqidong.github.io. Anti-case: nileshsuri.github.io, where the news feed *replaces* the publication list.
9. **One accent color at most, on a white background; color comes from content images, not chrome.** jonbarron.info (blue links only), ysymyth.github.io (monochrome + blue), hangzhaomit.github.io, danqic, wenzhuo-liu.github.io, colinraffel.com (grayscale photo). huang-zilin.com limits accent to the burgundy Sky-Lab logo.
10. **A rigid, repeated card template for every work item.** hangzhaomit.github.io (thumbnail → title → authors → venue/year → one italic sentence → Paper/Code/Project, repeated identically), jonbarron.info, rush-nlp.com, carlinds.github.io. The rhythm is what makes long lists readable.
11. **One plain-language sentence per paper explaining why it matters.** jonbarron.info and hangzhaomit.github.io both do this; it is rare and it is the biggest readability win available.
12. **Consistent institutional/affiliation logos, used sparingly.** hangzhaomit.github.io (logo gallery at the bottom), zihaosheng.github.io (inline UW–Madison / NVIDIA / Bosch badges), huang-zilin.com (UW–Madison, Purdue, CCAT, SHRC, TRAVELS), colinraffel.com (Toronto, Vector, HF as text).
13. **An explicit, early "what I'm looking for" line.** cbfinn (prospective-students note near the top), huang-zilin.com ("on the 2026–2027 academic job market"), ys-qu.github.io (internship CTA), yongqidong.github.io (recruitment statement), colinraffel.com (how to join the lab).
14. **Personal material has substance, not a placeholder.** yongqidong.github.io Miscellany (vegetarian/sustainable lifestyle, Tai Chi, meditation, three quotes), ysymyth.github.io "recent readings" (philosophy, physics, cognitive science), maithraraghu.com (maths olympiads), rush-nlp.com and colinraffel.com (self-deprecating asides). Note the pattern: these are *specific*, and none of them are emoji-driven.
15. **Emoji are near-absent from the top-tier pages.** None of jonbarron.info, ysymyth.github.io, rush-nlp.com, colinraffel.com, cbfinn, danqic, hangzhaomit.github.io, carlinds.github.io use emoji in the bio. Emoji clusters are concentrated in the CN/ITS student pages (huang-zilin.com, zihaosheng.github.io, he-h.github.io, yongqidong.github.io) — it is a subfield convention, not a mark of quality, and it reads as junior at density.

## 2. Anti-patterns on weaker pages

- **Publication list as a news feed.** nileshsuri.github.io announces papers as dated bulletins; there is no portfolio view.
- **Delegating publications entirely off-site.** colinraffel.com says "check arXiv" — zero curation, and the visitor learns nothing about what matters.
- **The HTML-CV.** he-h.github.io and yongqidong.github.io stack Education → Awards → Talks → Teaching → Service on the homepage; the page becomes a résumé transcription instead of an argument.
- **Nav inflation.** 8–10 items (huang-zilin.com, ys-qu.github.io, he-h.github.io) for a body of work that fits on two pages.
- **"Selected" that isn't selected.** 9–12 entries under a "selected" heading (huang-zilin.com, carlinds.github.io, mczhi.github.io).
- **Photo demoted below the fold or displaced by a decorative graphic.** danqic (headshot after the bio), ys-qu.github.io (handwritten signature occupies the hero slot).
- **Dated blog chrome** — sidebars, comment counts, pagination (timedettmers.com).
- **Regional-only credibility signals** — impact factors, CCF/JCR ranks, "Friendly Links", visitor counters (wenzhuo-liu.github.io, huang-zilin.com's visitor stat). These carry little weight with US faculty readers and cost hero real estate.
- **Zero imagery in a visual field.** nileshsuri.github.io works on AVs and traffic optimization and shows not one figure.
- **Conflating "projects" and "publications"** without explaining the distinction (rush-nlp.com, hangzhaomit.github.io).
- **Broken/abandoned reference links** — even the official al-folio showcase has rotted entries (platanios.org is now a gambling site), so the showcase should be treated as a starting point, not an endorsement.

## 3. Field-specific notes for transportation / AV / ITS pages

- **Animated GIF thumbnails are the field norm among the best pages and are near-mandatory.** carlinds.github.io, ys-qu.github.io, zihaosheng.github.io, hangzhaomit.github.io all lead publication entries with motion. Static diagrams (wenzhuo-liu.github.io, mczhi.github.io) are a clear step down: a driving policy, a merge maneuver, or a trajectory prediction is legible in two seconds of loop and illegible as prose.
- **Simulator screenshots are used as first-class evidence** (ys-qu.github.io explicitly; carlinds.github.io via neural-rendering/3DGS reconstructions). CARLA/SUMO/MetaDrive frames tell a reader what the experimental substrate is.
- **Maps and network/corridor visualizations are conspicuously rare** — none of the surveyed pages foreground them, even in the ITS group. This is an open differentiation opportunity for a transportation-engineering student whose work touches corridors or networks.
- **Venue badges do double duty in this field** because the venue set is split across two cultures: transportation journals (TR-C, TRB, JICV, T-ITS) and CV/ML conferences (CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS). huang-zilin.com, zihaosheng.github.io and carlinds.github.io all badge both, which is exactly how a cross-disciplinary reader is reassured.
- **GitHub star counts on code releases** appear on zihaosheng.github.io and mczhi.github.io and are a credible, field-appropriate impact signal for simulator/toolkit work — more persuasive than citation counts for a first-year.
- **A research-vision figure is the single largest visual differentiator in this group.** Only huang-zilin.com has one, and it is the main reason that page reads as more mature than its peers.
- **Emoji and WeChat/QR links are a strong convention in the CN-origin ITS cohort** (huang-zilin.com, ys-qu.github.io, zihaosheng.github.io, he-h.github.io, wenzhuo-liu.github.io) — worth keeping at low density for the audience it serves, but it should not dominate the bio.
- **Job-market / internship-seeking statements are standard and placed early** (huang-zilin.com, ys-qu.github.io, yongqidong.github.io).

## 4. Gap list — the user's current site (https://zhengyangwan.com/) vs. these traits

**Already satisfied:**
- **Short nav (4 items):** Home / Publications / Projects / About me — matches carlinds.github.io (3), zihaosheng.github.io (3), jasonwei.net (4), maithraraghu.com (4). Do not add items.
- **Genuinely selected publications (4)** — stricter than huang-zilin.com (9), carlinds.github.io (11), mczhi.github.io (12). This is a real advantage.
- **Publication thumbnails present** (landscape research previews), aligning with jonbarron.info, carlinds.github.io, rush-nlp.com.
- **News as 4 terse dated lines**, matching huang-zilin.com, carlinds.github.io, markdean.info.
- **Photo is right-floated and modest**, in line with the ≤30% convention (jonbarron.info, ysymyth.github.io).
- **White background, essentially no accent color** — matches the monochrome-plus-link-color norm across jonbarron.info, ysymyth.github.io, hangzhaomit.github.io, danqic.
- **Institutional logos inline** (UW–Madison, Sky-Lab, Tongji), as on zihaosheng.github.io and huang-zilin.com.
- **Multiple profile links present** (Email, CV, Scholar, ORCID, GitHub, LinkedIn, WeChat) — six-to-seven is the healthy range (jasonwei.net 4, jonbarron.info 6, zihaosheng.github.io 9); huang-zilin.com's 11 is excessive.
- **Education + Service sections exist** — appropriate for a first-year, though see below on their position.

**Not yet satisfied:**
- **No tagline.** The hero currently goes name → "Hello there!🤺" → bio. There is no equivalent of "I study agents" (ysymyth.github.io), "Autonomous Driving | Foundation Models | RL" (zihaosheng.github.io), or "Making deep learning accessible." (timdettmers.com). This is the largest single gap and the cheapest to close.
- **No research-overview block and no research hero figure.** This is the trait that most distinguishes the reference site (huang-zilin.com's full-width ecosystem diagram + three numbered research questions) from the user's page. The user has a Research block, but it lives on the *Publications* page rather than the homepage, and it has no figure.
- **No demo GIFs or simulator screenshots anywhere**, while every strong AV peer uses them (carlinds.github.io, ys-qu.github.io, zihaosheng.github.io, hangzhaomit.github.io). Static WebP previews are the current state.
- **No venue badges on publication entries.** Peers badge consistently (huang-zilin.com, carlinds.github.io, zihaosheng.github.io, mczhi.github.io). Venue text may be present but is not treated as a distinct visual token.
- **No one-sentence "why this paper matters" line per entry** — the trait that makes jonbarron.info and hangzhaomit.github.io outstanding, and which almost nobody in the ITS cohort does.
- **No "selected → view all" affordance** on the homepage publications block; zihaosheng.github.io is the model.
- **No explicit availability/intent statement** (internship-seeking, collaboration interests), which cbfinn, huang-zilin.com, ys-qu.github.io and yongqidong.github.io all place early.
- **Emoji density is high in the bio** ("Hello there!🤺", 🧐, 🏎️💨, 🥳) where the top-tier pages use none in the bio (jonbarron.info, ysymyth.github.io, rush-nlp.com, colinraffel.com, carlinds.github.io). Keeping them in *News* — as huang-zilin.com does — is the field-consistent compromise.
- **"About me" is a hobbies/travel placeholder**, whereas the pages that do this well make it specific and substantive: yongqidong.github.io's Miscellany, ysymyth.github.io's recent readings, maithraraghu.com's olympiad note. A placeholder page is worse than no page.
- **No per-paper resource link row beyond Abs/paper/BibTeX** — peers consistently offer project page / code / video / poster (carlinds.github.io, ys-qu.github.io, maithraraghu.com, zihaosheng.github.io).
- **Education and Service currently sit on the homepage below Selected Publications**, pushing the page toward the HTML-CV anti-pattern seen on he-h.github.io and yongqidong.github.io. The strongest peers (carlinds.github.io, markdean.info, maithraraghu.com) keep the homepage to identity → research → news → selected work and move résumé material elsewhere.
- **Projects page uses cards but is not visually tied to the publication template.** hangzhaomit.github.io's strength is one identical card template everywhere; the user currently has two different visual languages (cards on Projects, list-with-thumbnails on Publications).
- **No stated distinction between "Projects" and "Publications"** — the same ambiguity that weakens rush-nlp.com and hangzhaomit.github.io.

**现状 → 建议（按影响排序）**

| 维度 | 现状（截图/源码） | 为什么不够"高级" | 建议 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **字体** | 3 族：Source Serif 4（标题+正文）、Inter（导航/副标）、JetBrains Mono（日期、`ctrl k`、`GOOGLE SCHOLAR 23`、`ABS/PAPER` 按钮） | 三族混用 + 大量等宽大写标签，观感偏"技术仪表盘"而非"出版物" | 降到 2 族：**衬线只做名字和章节标题（display），正文与 UI 全用 Inter**；等宽只保留 News 日期一处（或干脆也用 Inter 的表格数字）。正文 1.0625rem、行高 1.6、字重 400，少用加粗 |
| **颜色** | 白底 + 墨色 #141413 + 灰 #6B6B6A + 铁锈 #B3654A；但 venue 徽章是洋红/赭黄、统计 pill 是纯黑色块、`Scholar 0` 黑块、顶部橙色进度条 | 页面上最抢眼的颜色来自徽章和黑块，而不是内容 | 全站只允许 **墨 / 灰 / 白 + 一个强调色**，且强调色每屏 ≤3 处（当前导航下划线、链接 hover）。venue 徽章改为**浅灰底深灰字的小标签**或纯文字；统计 pill 改成一行灰字 `23 citations · 9 GitHub stars`；引用为 0 不显示；进度条关掉 |
| **版心与字号** | `max_width: 1080px`，正文行长约 95–100 字符；名字 2.5rem 粗体；章节标题 1.75rem 半粗（几乎与页标题一样大） | 行太长读起来累，层级压得太扁，"大字加粗"显得用力 | 版心收到 **960px**，正文区最大 **68ch**；名字 2.25rem 字重 500；章节标题 1.375rem 字重 500；层级靠字号差 + 留白，不靠加粗 |
| **首页布局** | 头像右浮在 bio 里，文字先 65% 宽再变全宽（参差）；图标 7 个 1.6rem 一排 | 段落宽度变化、图标偏大偏满 | 改成**两栏 hero**：左列名字/副标/图标/bio（固定 68ch），右列头像顶对齐、宽 ~220px、圆角 6px、无阴影；图标 1.25rem、更灰、间距更大 |
| **组件** | `ABS` `PAPER` 描边大写按钮；缩略图带阴影；`ctrl k` 搜索 pill；固定深色页脚；ClustrMaps 热图；News 日期等宽 | 按钮/阴影/黑条都是"界面感"元素 | 论文链接改为小号灰字 `PDF · Code · Abstract`（hover 变强调色）；缩略图统一 4:3、1px 极细边、无阴影；搜索只留一个图标；页脚改为页尾浅色一行小字；去掉热图 |
| **留白节奏** | 章节间 32px（去线后略挤） | 无分割线的极简风靠留白分区 | 章节间 48px、标题下 20px、列表项 8px；整体"稀疏一点"是高级感的主要来源 |

**字体方向：正文用什么？**

Options:
- **衬线标题 + Inter 正文 (Recommended)** - 名字、章节标题、论文标题用 Source Serif 4；正文、导航、列表、按钮用 Inter；等宽只留 News 日期。最接近“编辑排版 / 高级简约”。
- **全衬线（保持现状，只去等宽）** - 书籍感更强；去掉 UI 里的等宽标签即可。
- **全无衬线（Inter）** - 最克制、最“科技公司”；名字也用 Inter 500。

**强调色：目前是铁锈色 #B3654A（链接、导航下划线、About me 标题短横线）。**

Options:
- **保留铁锈色，但大幅克制使用 (Recommended)** - 正文链接改为墨色 + 1px 下划线，hover 时才变铁锈色；强调色只用在导航当前项、hover、标题短横线。保留识别度。
- **换成中性深蓝/石墨色** - 例如 #1F3A5F 或 #2F3437，更“学术正式”，但个性弱一些。
- **纯单色：不要强调色** - 墨/灰/白，链接靠下划线区分（jonbarron 风）。

**界面减负：以下哪些同意在本批一起改？** _(select multiple)_

Options:
- **去掉顶部阅读进度条 + “ctrl k”文字（只留搜索图标）** - enable_progressbar: false；搜索入口改为单个图标。
- **固定深色页脚 → 页尾浅色一行小字，并移除 ClustrMaps** - footer_fixed: false；页脚改为灰字 “© 2026 Zhengyang Wan · Updated …”；删除访客热图。
- **论文条目去“界面感”：彩色 venue 徽章→浅灰小标签，描边按钮→灰色文字链接，统计 pill→一行灰字，缩略图去阴影** - 修改 bib.liquid 与对应 SCSS；信息不少，只是安静下来。
- **版心 1080→960px，正文限 68ch，名字/章节标题缩小并改为字重 500，首页改为两栏 hero（头像右列顶对齐），章节间距 48px** - 改 _config.yml max_width、_tokens/_base/_layout 的字号字重与间距、about.liquid 的 hero 结构。


**Answer:** 衬线标题 + Inter 正文 (Recommended), 保留铁锈色，但大幅克制使用 (Recommended), 版心 1080→960px，正文限 68ch，名字/章节标题缩小并改为字重 500，首页改为两栏 hero（头像右列顶对齐），章节间距 48px, 去掉顶部阅读进度条 + “ctrl k”文字（只留搜索图标）, 论文条目去“界面感”：彩色 venue 徽章→浅灰小标签，描边按钮→灰色文字链接，统计 pill→一行灰字，缩略图去阴影

# 网站改版：简约高级风格（结构 + 视觉系统 + 清理）

## Context

用户要求：调研优秀 PhD/研究员主页风格，结合当前内容给出审美/排版改进方向，目标是"简约高级"。调研覆盖 18 个站点（jonbarron、ysymyth、jasonwei、rush-nlp、colinraffel、cbfinn 等 ML 页；huang-zilin（参考站）、zihaosheng/ys-qu（Sky-Lab 同门）、carlinds、hangzhaomit 等 AV/ITS 页；al-folio showcase），并用 Chrome 截图线上 4 页、审计源码。

用户已拍板：
- 结构：Education/Service 移到 About me；首页加带图 Research 区块（用 Projects 页 Sky-Drive 总图）；Star Trek 引言保留、其余模板遗留清理；bio 去 emoji、不加定位语。
- 视觉：**衬线只做标题（Source Serif 4），正文/UI 用 Inter，等宽只留 News 日期**；**铁锈色保留但克制**（正文链接墨色下划线，hover 才变色）；版心 1080→960、正文 68ch、名字/章节标题缩小并改字重 500、首页两栏 hero、章节间距 48px；去顶部进度条 + "ctrl k" 文字；论文条目去界面感（彩色 venue 徽章→浅灰小标签、描边按钮→灰色文字链接、统计 pill→一行灰字、缩略图去阴影）。
- 不动：固定深色页脚、ClustrMaps（列入后续可选）。

## 一、调研结论（共性）
1. 首页 = 身份 → 研究概述（带一张图） → News（3–5） → 精选论文（≤5 + view all）；简历材料放子页。
2. 研究愿景图是最大差异化因素（参考站的核心优势）；AV 圈用 GIF/模拟器截图做缩略图。
3. 导航 3–5 项、"Selected" 真的少（已达标）。每条论文：缩略图 + 粗体本人名 + venue 标签（已有）。
4. 白底、单强调色、颜色来自内容图；顶级页面 bio 不用 emoji。
5. 反模式：占位/示例内容上线、界面感元素（黑色 pill、彩色徽章、描边按钮、进度条）、三种字体混用、行长过长、大字加粗。

## 二、问题清单
**P0 bug**：CI 未装 ImageMagick → `-480.webp` 等 404，`<picture>` 不回退 → Publications Research 配图、About me 照片位空白框；图片体积失控（头像 webp 3.2 MB 且不走响应式、drivingsimulator.jpg 5.9 MB、fig1.svg 8 MB、VRU.png 1.7 MB、skylab.png 0.7 MB、两张论文预览 1.3 MB+）；占位/示例内容已上线并进入全站搜索索引（About me 占位、skydrive/VRU 项目示例正文且 VRU redirect 到 unsplash、/teaching/ /repositories/ /people/ 可访问）。
**P1 结构**：研究兴趣分散两处、无概述图；Education/Service 在首页底部；bio emoji；精选论文无 "All publications"；引用 0 显示 "Scholar 0"。
**P1 视觉**：三族字体 + 等宽大写标签；徽章/黑块/进度条抢色；1080 版心行长 ~95 字符；名字 2.5rem 粗体、章节标题 1.75rem 几乎与页标题同级；头像右浮导致段落宽度参差；按钮/阴影/热图等界面感元素。

# 网站改版：简约高级风格（结构 + 视觉系统 + 清理）

## Context

用户要求：调研优秀 PhD/研究员主页风格，结合当前内容给出审美/排版改进方向，目标是"简约高级"。调研覆盖 18 个站点（jonbarron、ysymyth、jasonwei、rush-nlp、colinraffel、cbfinn 等 ML 页；huang-zilin（参考站）、zihaosheng/ys-qu（Sky-Lab 同门）、carlinds、hangzhaomit 等 AV/ITS 页；al-folio showcase），并用 Chrome 截图线上 4 页、审计源码。

用户已拍板：
- 结构：Education/Service 移到 About me；首页加带图 Research 区块（用 Projects 页 Sky-Drive 总图）；Star Trek 引言保留、其余模板遗留清理；bio 去 emoji、不加定位语。
- 视觉：**衬线只做标题（Source Serif 4），正文/UI 用 Inter，等宽只留 News 日期**；**铁锈色保留但克制**（正文链接墨色下划线，hover 才变色）；版心 1080→960、正文 68ch、名字/章节标题缩小并改字重 500、首页两栏 hero、章节间距 48px；去顶部进度条 + "ctrl k" 文字；论文条目去界面感（彩色 venue 徽章→浅灰小标签、描边按钮→灰色文字链接、统计 pill→一行灰字、缩略图去阴影）。
- 不动：固定深色页脚、ClustrMaps（列入后续可选）。

## 一、调研结论（共性）
1. 首页 = 身份 → 研究概述（带一张图） → News（3–5） → 精选论文（≤5 + view all）；简历材料放子页。
2. 研究愿景图是最大差异化因素（参考站的核心优势）；AV 圈用 GIF/模拟器截图做缩略图。
3. 导航 3–5 项、"Selected" 真的少（已达标）。每条论文：缩略图 + 粗体本人名 + venue 标签（已有）。
4. 白底、单强调色、颜色来自内容图；顶级页面 bio 不用 emoji。
5. 反模式：占位/示例内容上线、界面感元素（黑色 pill、彩色徽章、描边按钮、进度条）、三种字体混用、行长过长、大字加粗。

## 二、问题清单
**P0 bug**：CI 未装 ImageMagick → `-480.webp` 等 404，`<picture>` 不回退 → Publications Research 配图、About me 照片位空白框；图片体积失控（头像 webp 3.2 MB 且不走响应式、drivingsimulator.jpg 5.9 MB、fig1.svg 8 MB、VRU.png 1.7 MB、skylab.png 0.7 MB、两张论文预览 1.3 MB+）；占位/示例内容已上线并进入全站搜索索引（About me 占位、skydrive/VRU 项目示例正文且 VRU redirect 到 unsplash、/teaching/ /repositories/ /people/ 可访问）。
**P1 结构**：研究兴趣分散两处、无概述图；Education/Service 在首页底部；bio emoji；精选论文无 "All publications"；引用 0 显示 "Scholar 0"。
**P1 视觉**：三族字体 + 等宽大写标签；徽章/黑块/进度条抢色；1080 版心行长 ~95 字符；名字 2.5rem 粗体、章节标题 1.75rem 几乎与页标题同级；头像右浮导致段落宽度参差；按钮/阴影/热图等界面感元素。
