      -webkit-box-orient: vertical;
      overflow: hidden;
    }

    &:hover .card-title {
      color: var(--global-theme-color);
    }
  }

  .project-tags {
    display: flex;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    gap: $sp-1 $sp-2;
    margin-bottom: $sp-2;
    padding: 0;
    list-style: none;

    li {
      font-family: $ff-mono;
      font-size: $fs-xs;
      color: var(--mono-meta-color);
      padding: 0 $sp-2;
      border: 1px solid var(--hairline);
      border-radius: $r-md;
      background: var(--global-bg-subtle);
      letter-spacing: 0.02em;
    }
  }

  .project-meta {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: space-between;
    font-family: $ff-mono;
    font-size: $fs-xs;
    color: var(--mono-meta-color);

    .github-icon {
      display: inline-flex;
      align-items: center;
      gap: $sp-2;

      a {
        color: inherit;
      }

      .stars {
        display: inline-flex;
        align-items: center;
        gap: $sp-1;
      }
    }
  }

  .col {
    padding-bottom: $sp-4;
  }

  .grid-sizer,
  .grid-item {
    width: 250px;
    margin-bottom: $sp-3;
  }

  // Legacy heading — kept for backward compat but visually minimal.
  h2.category {
    display: none;
  }
}

// Filter chips row (replaces h2.category).
.filter-chips {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  gap: $sp-2;
  margin: $sp-5 0 $sp-5;
  padding-bottom: $sp-3;

  a {
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    padding: $sp-1 $sp-3;
    font-family: $ff-sans;
    font-size: $fs-xs;
    font-weight: $fw-semibold;
    letter-spacing: 0.04em;
    text-transform: uppercase;
    color: var(--mono-meta-color);
    background: transparent;
    border: 1px solid var(--hairline);
    border-radius: $r-pill;
    text-decoration: none;
    transition:
      color $dur-base $ease-out,
      border-color $dur-base $ease-out,
      background $dur-base $ease-out;

    &:hover,
    &.active {
      color: var(--global-theme-color);
      border-color: var(--global-theme-color);
      background: transparent;
      text-decoration: none;
    }
  }
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Publications — Academic Editorial with mono metadata accents.
//
// Layout: year headers act as sticky gutter labels on desktop (≥992px) and
// inline headers on mobile. Each paper is a hairline row — no boxed card.
// Thumbnails are small, left-aligned; links are hairline pills; Scholar /
// GitHub counts live in mono stat pills on the right.
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

.publications {
  margin-top: $sp-4;

  h1 {
    color: var(--global-text-color);
    font-family: $ff-serif;
    font-size: $fs-2xl;
    font-weight: $fw-semibold;
    text-align: left;
    margin: $sp-6 0 $sp-4;
  }

  // Row of stat pills (sits above the bibsearch + bibliography).
  .stat-pill-row {
    display: flex;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    gap: $sp-3;
    align-items: center;
    margin: $sp-3 0 $sp-4;
  }

  // Research interests block (image left, interest lists right).
  .research-interests {
    margin: 0 0 $sp-4;
    padding-bottom: $sp-4;

    .research-interests__title {
      font-family: $ff-serif;
      font-size: $fs-xl;
      font-weight: $fw-semibold;
      text-align: center;
      margin: 0 0 $sp-4;
    }

    figure {
      margin: 0;
    }

    .research-interests__group {
      font-family: $ff-sans;
      font-size: $fs-base;
      font-weight: $fw-semibold;
      margin: 0 0 $sp-1;
    }

    ul {
      list-style: disc;
      padding-left: 1.2em;
      margin: 0 0 $sp-3;

      li {
        font-family: $ff-serif;
        line-height: $lh-body;
        margin-bottom: $sp-1;
      }
    }

    ul:last-child {
      margin-bottom: 0;
    }
  }

  // Stat pill (Scholar total / GitHub total at top of publications page).
  // No outer border — the two-tone (label bg + value bg) halves carry the
  // visual weight; an extra hairline around them reads as a redundant frame.
  .stat-pill {
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: stretch;
    text-decoration: none;
    border-radius: $r-md;
    overflow: hidden;
    font-family: $ff-mono;
    line-height: 1;

    .stat-pill__label {
      display: inline-flex;
      align-items: center;
      gap: $sp-2;
      padding: $sp-2 $sp-3;
      font-size: $fs-xs;
      font-weight: $fw-semibold;
      color: var(--global-text-color);
      background: var(--global-bg-subtle);
      text-transform: uppercase;
      letter-spacing: 0.04em;

      i { font-size: 1em; }
    }

    .stat-pill__value {
      display: inline-flex;
      align-items: center;
      padding: $sp-2 $sp-3;
      font-size: $fs-xs;
      font-weight: $fw-bold;
      color: var(--global-bg-color);
      background: var(--global-text-color);
    }
  }

  // Year group header (jekyll-scholar emits <h2 class="bibliography">YEAR</h2>).
```

33	  preview={drivevlmrl.webp},
34	  abstract={Ensuring safe decision-making in autonomous vehicles remains a fundamental challenge despite rapid advances in end-to-end learning approaches. Traditional reinforcement learning (RL) methods rely on manually engineered rewards or sparse collision signals, which fail to capture the rich contextual understanding required for safe driving and make unsafe exploration unavoidable in real-world settings. Recent vision-language models (VLMs) offer promising semantic understanding capabilities; however, their high inference latency and susceptibility to hallucination hinder direct application to real-time vehicle control. To address these limitations, this paper proposes DriveVLM-RL, a neuroscience-inspired framework that integrates VLMs into RL through a dual-pathway architecture for safe and deployable autonomous driving. The framework decomposes semantic reward learning into a Static Pathway for continuous spatial safety assessment using CLIP-based contrasting language goals, and a Dynamic Pathway for attention-gated multi-frame semantic risk reasoning using a lightweight detector and a large VLM. A hierarchical reward synthesis mechanism fuses semantic signals with vehicle states, while an asynchronous training pipeline decouples expensive VLM inference from environment interaction. All VLM components are used only during offline training and are removed at deployment, ensuring real-time feasibility. Experiments in the CARLA simulator show significant improvements in collision avoidance, task success, and generalization across diverse traffic scenarios, including strong robustness under settings without explicit collision penalties. These results demonstrate that DriveVLM-RL provides a practical paradigm for integrating foundation models into autonomous driving without compromising real-time feasibility.},
35	  annotation={* Equal Contribution<br>✉ Corresponding Author},
36	  selected={true}

However, existing simulators do not yet fully meet the needs of future transportation research, particularly in modeling socially-aware driving agents and enabling effective human-AI collaboration. This paper introduces Sky-Drive, a novel distributed multi-agent simulation platform that addresses these limitations through four key innovations: (a) a distributed architecture for synchronized simulation across multiple terminals; (b) a multi-modal human-in-the-loop framework integrating diverse sensors to collect rich behavioral data; (c) a human-AI collaboration mechanism supporting continuous and adaptive knowledge exchange; and (d) a digital twin (DT) framework for constructing high-fidelity virtual replicas of real-world transportation environments. Sky-Drive supports diverse applications such as autonomous vehicle (AV)-vulnerable road user (VRU) interaction modeling, human-in-the-loop training, socially-aware reinforcement learning, personalized driving policy, and customized scenario generation. Future extensions will incorporate foundation models for context-aware decision support and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing for real-world validation. 67	  abstract={The Virtual Track Train (VTT) represents a novel urban transportation solution that combines elements of both road and rail vehicles. Currently, VTT has gained significant adoption in several cities in China including Yibin, Zhuzhou, Harbin, and Yancheng. Despite its growing usage, the unique structure and complex tire-ground interaction of VTT pose significant challenges in terms of tire wear, which has become a pressing issue. This study develops and validates a multi-body dynamics model of VTT along with a finite element model of its tire. The tire-ground contact behavior and boundary conditions are studied from various perspectives to calculate tire wear. The simulation results demonstrate that the internal pressure of the tires, the load of VTT, the pavement conditions, the inclination angle, and slippage of tires all have critical effects on VTT’s tire wear. These findings suggest that the operating conditions of VTT must be carefully managed to reduce tire wear and ensure safe operation. Furthermore, the research results of tire wear mechanism of VTT offers valuable insights for the optimization and maintenance of VTT.},

from PIL import Image, ImageChops
im = Image.open('$SCRATCH/fig_chrome.png').convert('RGB')
bg = Image.new('RGB', im.size, (255,255,255))
diff = ImageChops.difference(im, bg)
bbox = diff.getbbox()
print('bbox', bbox)
if bbox:
    # add small padding
    pad = 15
    l,t,r,b = bbox
    l = max(0, l-pad); t = max(0, t-pad)
    r = min(im.width, r+pad); b = min(im.height, b+pad)
    cropped = im.crop((l,t,r,b))
    print('cropped size', cropped.size)
    cropped.save('$SCRATCH/fig_cropped.png')
"

---
layout: page
title: SkyDrive
description: SkyDrive is a multi-agent human-in-the-loop, digital-twin-enabled traffic simulator.
img: assets/img/research_overview.jpg
importance: 1
category: UW-Madison
related_publications: true
---

Sky-Drive is a distributed multi-agent simulation platform developed at Sky-Lab for socially-aware and human-AI collaborative future transportation research. It combines a multi-modal human-in-the-loop framework, a human-AI collaboration mechanism, and a digital-twin framework for building high-fidelity virtual replicas of real-world transportation environments, supporting applications such as AV-VRU interaction modeling, socially-aware reinforcement learning, and personalized driving policy.

The platform is open source and available on GitHub: [Sky-Drive](https://github.com/BillWan-zzzyyy/Sky-Drive).

```

## Per-file changes

**`_sass/_tokens.scss`** — `$fs-2xl: 2.5rem → 2.25rem`.

**`_sass/_base.scss`**
- A1: `body` → `$ff-sans` / `1.0625rem` / `$lh-body`; h1/h2 weight `$fw-semibold → $fw-medium`; h3 switched `$ff-sans → $ff-serif` + `$fw-medium` (plan §A1 says serif = h1–h3).
- A1 serif→sans: `.news-body`, `.post-description`, `.projects .card-text`, `.publications .author`.
- A1 mono→sans: `.social .contact-note`, `.tag-category-list p,li`, `.project-tags li`, `.project-meta`, `.publications h2.bibliography`, `.more-authors`, `.periodical`, `.badge-pill`. Also dropped the legacy `font-family: monospace` on `.profile .more-info`.
- A1 weights: `.post-header .post-title`, `.publications h1`, `.publications .title` → `$fw-medium`; `.post-header` margin-bottom `$sp-5 → $sp-6`.
- A2: global `a, table.table a` → ink + 1px hairline underline, 3px offset, hover → accent + `currentColor`; deleted the stray `&:hover:after :not(...)` rule. Explicit `text-decoration: none` added to `.navbar.navbar-light a`, `.navbar-brand`, `.social .contact-icons a`, `.news-title`, `.pub-links a`, `.badge-pill`, and both footer link rules (footer fonts untouched). `.publications .author a` lost its border-bottom (now uses the global underline).
- A5: `.abbr abbr` → grey `--global-bg-subtle` uppercase tag (with `!important` to beat any residual inline color); `.preview` + `.preview img` → 4/3, hairline, `$r-md`, no shadow; `.links a.btn` block replaced by `.pub-links a` (grey sans text links, `+ a::before { content: '·' }`); `.badge-pill` flattened to the same grey chip; new `.publications .pub-stats` (sans, `$fs-sm`, grey, `margin: 0 0 $sp-5`).
- Deleted: `.publications .research-interests {…}`, all `.stat-pill*` rules and `.stat-pill-row`, and the whole `#search-toggle .search-pill` block. `#light-toggle, #search-toggle` gained `i { font-size: 1.1rem }` so search matches the theme icon.

===== about.liquid (full)
---
layout: default
---
<div class="post">
  <!-- Hero: identity + bio on the left, portrait on the right -->
  <div class="about-hero">
    <div class="about-hero__text">
      <header class="post-header about-header">
        <h1 class="post-title about-title">
          {% if site.title == 'blank' %}
            <span class="font-weight-bold">{{ site.first_name }}</span> {{ site.middle_name }}
            {{ site.last_name }}
          {% else %}
            {{ site.title }}
          {% endif %}
        </h1>

        <div class="desc about-subtitle">{{ page.subtitle }}</div>

        <!-- Social -->
        {% if page.social %}
          <div class="social" style="text-align: left; margin-top: 0.5rem;">
            <div class="contact-icons">{% include social.liquid %}</div>
            <div class="contact-note">{{ site.contact_note }}</div>
          </div>
        {% endif %}

        {% if site.newsletter.enabled and site.footer_fixed %}
          {% include scripts/newsletter.liquid center=true %}
        {% endif %}
      </header>

      <div class="bio">{{ content }}</div>
    </div>

    {% if page.profile %}
      <div class="about-hero__media">
        <div class="profile">
          <div class="profile__card">
            {% if page.profile.image %}
              {% assign profile_image_path = page.profile.image | prepend: 'assets/img/' %}
              {% if page.profile.image_circular %}
                {% assign profile_image_class = 'img-fluid rounded-circle' %}
              {% else %}
                {% assign profile_image_class = 'img-fluid rounded' %}
              {% endif %}
              {% capture sizes %}(min-width: 768px) 220px, 160px{% endcapture %}
              {%
                include figure.liquid
                loading="eager"
                path=profile_image_path
                class=profile_image_class
                sizes=sizes
                alt=page.profile.image
                cache_bust=true
              %}
            {% endif %}
            {% if page.profile.more_info %}
              <div class="more-info">{{ page.profile.more_info }}</div>
            {% endif %}
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    {% endif %}
  </div>

  <article>
    <!-- Research -->
    {% if page.research %}
      <section class="home-section research-block">
        <h6>Research</h6>
        {% assign rpath = page.research.image | prepend: 'assets/img/' %}
        {% include figure.liquid path=rpath class="img-fluid rounded research-block__figure" alt=page.research.alt zoomable=true %}
        <div class="row">
          {% for g in page.research.groups %}
            <div class="col-md-6">
              <p class="research-block__group">{{ g.title }}</p>
              <ul>
                {% for item in g.items %}
                  <li>{{ item }}</li>
                {% endfor %}
              </ul>
            </div>
          {% endfor %}
        </div>
      </section>
    {% endif %}

    <!-- Recent News -->
    {% if page.news and site.announcements.enabled %}
      <section class="home-section">
        <h6>
          <a href="{{ '/news/' | relative_url }}">Recent News</a>
        </h6>
        {% include news.liquid limit=true %}
      </section>
    {% endif %}

    <!-- Selected Publications -->
    {% if page.selected_papers %}
      <section class="home-section">
        <h6>
          <a href="{{ '/publications/' | relative_url }}">Selected Publications</a>
        </h6>
        {% include selected_papers.liquid %}
        <p class="home-more">
          <a href="{{ '/publications/' | relative_url }}">All publications →</a>
        </p>
      </section>
    {% endif %}
  </article>

  <!-- Visitor heatmap ornament (muted, low emphasis) -->
  <div class="footer__ornament" aria-hidden="true">
    <div style="transform: scale(0.7); transform-origin: top center;">
      <script type='text/javascript' id='clustrmaps' src='//clustrmaps.com/map_v2.js?d=iWTm2HbayeimtnXDADURqs5_Im3_wek8M_WS3lq5qLI&cl=ffffff&w=a'></script>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

===== about.md (full)
---
layout: about
title: Home
permalink: /
subtitle: <span class="highlight-text"> Ph.D. student </span>at The University of Wisconsin-Madison CEE


profile:
  align: right
  image: profile.jpg
  image_circular: false # crops the image to make it circular
  more_info: >
    <p>Chicago, US, 2025</p>

news: true # includes a list of news items
selected_papers: true # includes a list of papers marked as "selected={true}"
social: true # includes social icons at the bottom of the page

research:
  image: research_overview.jpg   # rendered from the Sky-Drive framework figure (fig1.svg)
  alt: Sky-Drive framework — multi-agent simulation, digital twin, and human-AI collaboration
  groups:
    - title: Autonomous driving
      items:
        - Closed-loop simulation and sim-to-real transfer
        - Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for driving
    - title: Human-centric intelligent transportation
      items:
        - Human-AI collaborative driving and interaction
        - Socially-aware multi-agent systems
---
Hello there!

I am a first-year **Ph.D. student** in the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering at the <img src="../assets/img/uwmadison.png" class="inline-logo" alt="UW–Madison"/>[University of Wisconsin-Madison](https://www.wisc.edu/) (UW-Madison). I joined <img src="../assets/img/skylab.png" class="inline-logo" alt="Sky-Lab"/>[Sky-Lab](https://sky-lab-uw.github.io/) at UW-Madison in Fall 2025 under the guidance of Dr.[Sikai (Sky) Chen](https://sky-lab-uw.github.io/people/). On Wisconsin!<img src="../assets/img/bucky.png" class="inline-logo" alt="Bucky"/>

An equally important dimension of my work is to validate autonomous driving related methods through real‑vehicle testing: I have contributed to the development of <img src="../assets/img/Sky-Drive.png" class="inline-logo" alt="SkyDrive"/>[SkyDrive](https://github.com/BillWan-zzzyyy/Sky-Drive), an open source multi-agent platform for future transportation system and autonomous driving by Sky-Lab.

---

Sky-Drive is a distributed multi-agent simulation platform developed at Sky-Lab for socially-aware and human-AI collaborative future transportation research. It combines a multi-modal human-in-the-loop framework, a human-AI collaboration mechanism, and a digital-twin framework for building high-fidelity virtual replicas of real-world transportation environments, supporting applications such as AV-VRU interaction modeling, socially-aware reinforcement learning, and personalized driving policy.

The platform is open source and available on GitHub: [Sky-Drive](https://github.com/BillWan-zzzyyy/Sky-Drive).
